description:
`make uat-execute` is a weaker, artifact-less re-implementation of the
sweep's execute leg. Verified on develop @ fc31f3604:

1. _handle_execute (tests/uat/_cli.py:386-441) duplicates the
   orchestrator's preflight->execute sequence but does NOT install the
   per-cell disk-floor watch (orchestrator.py:141-162), does NOT write
   cells.jsonl or the accounting sidecar, so it has weaker mid-sweep disk
   protection (partially addressed by uat-disk-gate-always-on) and
   produces no durable artifacts for `make uat-report`. Same config,
   silently different behavior from `make uat-sweep`.

2. Duplicated contracts: the cells.jsonl schema lives in two files with
   no shared codec (writer orchestrator.py:563-604, reader
   _cli.py:184-201); the sidecar filename convention is built by hand in
   both (_cli.py:166 vs orchestrator.py:558-560); _handle_stress
   (_cli.py:96-113) duplicates run_sweep_from_path's stress_overrides
   logic (orchestrator.py:683-692) which currently has zero production
   callers.

3. execute.py god-phase cleanups that fall out of unification:
   - _apply_submit_classification (execute.py:544-556) re-reads and
     re-classifies the same result JSON run_cell already classified
     (runner.py:256-260) -- duplicate policy application, second file
     read per cell;
   - _compatibility_pruned_for_config re-runs enumeration during
     abort-artifact emission (orchestrator.py:554-555) -- a second
     independent enumeration that can diverge from the one execute used;
     thread the actual enumeration through instead;
   - free-space checking exists in three variants (preflight gate,
     execute platform-boundary at execute.py:680-706, orchestrator
     per-cell wrapper) -- consolidate the measurement into one shared
     helper (the policy sites stay distinct);
   - dead code: matrix.py:84-86 placeholder tuple assignments,
     timeouts.py:114-131 env_without_pythonpath / iter_argv_for_log
     (zero callers, docstring claims a consumer that does not exist).

4. Prose-string abort contract: the orchestrator decides to emit abort
   artifacts via `"free space" in (result.abort_reason or "")`
   (orchestrator.py:263, :346). Replace with a typed abort-kind enum
   field on PhaseResult/ExecuteOutcome so rewording a message cannot
   change control flow. (Resume-manifest emission at those sites is gone
   after uat-resume-retirement-artifact-durability.)

work_units.notes: New tests/uat/cells_io.py owns write_cells_jsonl (moved from orchestrator._write_cells_jsonl, including _persist_cell_failure_context /_cell_log_tail/_cell_log_has_marker/FAILURE_TAIL_* constants), read_cells_jsonl (moved from _cli._handle_report's inline JSONL parsing), read_skipped_unreachable_sidecar (moved from _cli._read_skipped_unreachable_sidecar), and cells_accounting_path (the unified sidecar-filename convention). orchestrator.py and _cli.py now call into cells_io; on-disk content is byte-identical (verified via the existing write/read round-trip tests, updated to call cells_io directly). Deviation from the implementation note: atomic_write_text was NOT moved into cells_io.py -- report.py and validate.py are both outside this TODO's scope_limit.only_modify, and atomic_write_text is a generic primitive shared by five artifact types, not cells.jsonl-specific. cells_io.py imports it from report.py instead (`from tests.uat.phases.report import atomic_write_text`), which satisfies "cells_io owns the schema" and "orchestrator/_cli consume one codec" without an out-of-scope edit.
work_units.summary: Extract cells_io.py owning cells.jsonl + accounting-sidecar read/write (single schema definition); orchestrator and _cli consume it; sidecar path helper unified

work_units.notes: _handle_execute now scopes config.phases to [preflight?, execute] (preflight included only when the loaded config's own phases: list requests it, matching the prior gating) and calls orchestrator.run_sweep directly instead of hand-rolling preflight+execute. SweepResult gained two additive fields (`preflight`, `execute_outcome`) so _handle_execute can rebuild its stdout JSON summary from the phase loop's own result. Behavior improvement (per approach): uat-execute now gets the per-cell disk-floor watch and writes cells.jsonl + accounting sidecar, including abort-safe partial artifacts on a mid-execute disk-floor trip (a scenario the old standalone path never covered). Added the required parity test (test_uat_execute_and_execute_only_sweep_produce_identical_cells_jsonl in test_cli_dispatch.py): uat-execute and an execute-only sweep produce byte-identical cells.jsonl + sidecar for the same mocked run_cell.
work_units.summary: Route _handle_execute through the orchestrator single-phase path so uat-execute gets the disk watch and writes cells.jsonl + sidecar like a sweep; keep --databases-root/--no-cleanup semantics

work_units.notes: _handle_stress no longer hand-applies the platform/benchmark/scale replace() overrides; it builds a stress_overrides dict and calls run_sweep_from_path(config_path, stress_overrides=...), which already implemented the identical closed override set (previously zero production callers). Printed JSON shape unchanged (still omits abort_reason, unlike _handle_sweep's summary). Added test_stress_main_forwards_platform_benchmark_scale_as_stress_overrides since run_sweep_from_path's stress_overrides path had no direct test before this TODO made it load-bearing.
work_units.summary: Delete _handle_stress duplication: route through run_sweep_from_path(stress_overrides=...); keep CLI flags and behavior identical

work_units.notes: run_cell (runner.py:256-260) already classifies for submit before returning; _apply_submit_classification's mirror in _run_platform_benchmark was idempotent on an already-classified CellResult, so it was pure waste (second file read) for the real runner. Deleted _apply_submit_classification outright: submit classification is the runner's contract (documented in run_execute's docstring), and injected test runners must classify like run_cell does. An interim commit gated the mirror behind a runner_needs_submit_classification flag; the review follow-up removed the flag and the mirror entirely, and its sole consumer (test_execute_downgrades_passed_cell_with_query_failure_result) now mirrors run_cell's classify_for_submit/ submit_state_is_cell_failure sequence in its fake runner, keeping the fixture-JSON classification policy load-bearing in the test. Also removed matrix.py's SQL_PLATFORMS/DOCKER_PLATFORMS/DATAFRAME_PLATFORMS placeholder tuples (immediately overwritten before any read) and timeouts.py's env_without_pythonpath/iter_argv_for_log plus their tests (verified zero callers repo-wide via grep).
work_units.summary: Remove _apply_submit_classification double-application from execute.py; delete dead code (matrix.py placeholders, timeouts env_without_pythonpath/iter_argv_for_log)

work_units.notes: No live substring-driven control flow remained by the time this TODO started (the two `"free space" in abort_reason` matches left in the codebase are test assertions on message content, not branches -- superseded by earlier uat-status-taxonomy-exit-code-fixes / uat-disk-gate-always-on work). Added the typed field anyway per the binding implementation note, as forward-looking hardening: abort_kind: str | None on ExecuteOutcome (execute.py) and PreflightResult (preflight.py), values "disk_floor" / "docker_startup" / "docker_teardown" / "docker_required" / "local_platform_unreachable". Deviation: added on the two concrete subclasses rather than the shared PhaseResult base -- phases/__init__.py is outside this TODO's scope_limit.only_modify. Not threaded into cells.jsonl (anti_pattern compliance). Threaded execute's real enumeration into the disk-floor abort path: run_execute now annotates a propagating DiskFloorAbort with its actual compatibility_pruned tuple (mirroring the existing skipped_unreachable_count annotation), and orchestrator.run_sweep synthesizes an ExecuteOutcome from it instead of passing execute_outcome=None, so _emit_abort_artifacts no longer falls back to _compatibility_pruned_for_config's second, possibly-diverging re-enumeration for this path (that fallback stays correct/necessary for a genuine preflight-phase abort, where execute never ran). Regression test added: test_disk_floor_abort_threads_real_compatibility_pruned_without_reenumerating.
work_units.summary: Replace the 'free space' abort_reason substring checks with a typed abort_kind field; thread execute's actual enumeration into abort-artifact emission instead of re-enumerating
